Kagha is a wood elven druid in the Emerald Grove during Act One. She was Halsin's Second Druid, but has named herself First Druid in his absence. She started the Rite of Thorns to seal the Grove off, no matter the consequences.
“
A viper bares her fangs defending her brood. Is it not her nature to strike at invaders?
„
— Kagha, defending her actions

Overview

Personality

Kagha is willing to take drastic action to prove her authority over the Emerald Grove. She views the tiefling refugees as parasites and refers to them as devils and a rot to be cleansed.

Kagha justifies her violent actions as those of a watchful broodmother. As such, Kagha admires drow and duergar for their culture of aggressive self-preservation. If the player character is a drow or duergar, she approves of their presence, calling it a gift.

Involvement

Act One

 Zevlor requests the party's aid on dealing with the acting Archdruid of the Grove, Kagha. He explains that she and the other druids are preparing a ritual to seal off the Grove from the rest of the world, endangering the tiefling refugees.

Saving Arabella

Upon entering the Inner Sanctum for the first time, the party finds Kagha reprimanding a tiefling child named  Arabella for attempting to steal the  Idol of Silvanus. The party and another druid,  Rath, can intervene to ⁠save her. If the player character fails to persuade Kagha or decides to not intervene, Arabella attempts to run, and Kagha's snake  Teela bites her, killing her instantly.[1]

Investigate Kagha

The party can investigate and eventually confront Kagha. This must be done before  Halsin is rescued from the Goblin Camp. Otherwise, the quest is cancelled early.

Kagha's personal chest is hidden in a corner of the sanctum. Lockpicking it reveals a letter which advances ⁠Investigate Kagha and guides the party to a covert location in the Swamp, where they can learn Kagha is secretly planning to offer control of the Grove to the Shadow Druids of Cloakwood.

If the party returns and confronts Kagha about her plan, the Shadow Druids led by  Olodan reveal themselves and order Kagha to attack the party and everyone else in the Sanctum. Telling Kagha that the party will not stay in her way is considered an oathbreaking action for  Paladins of any Oath subclass.

The party can persuade Kagha to see her wrongs and instead side with the Grove's druids. This can be done by passing a number of Persuasion and Religion checks, or by having previoulsy read all of the frescos surrounding the sanctum. Doing so grants the ⁠A Story for the Ages to characters with the  Entertainer background.

If Kagha survives, she shows remorse for her actions, thanks the party and allows the tieflings to remain in the Grove for as long as they need. If the player character is a druid, she bestows them the title of Faithwarden and gifts them  Pale Oak.

If the Shadow Druids are killed before confronting Kagha, she does not abandon her plans but remains neutral (non-hostile) and does not order the tieflings to be killed. The druids and tieflings in the grove then behave as if Kagha was defeated. Any remaining druids stop their ritual and sit dejectedly;  Amek,  Xeph and  Rechel then come down into the grove to gawk as normal.

Kagha's fate

If the party does not kill Kagha themselves, her fate depends largely on whether she was persuaded to turn against the shadow druids, and whether Arabella died in her custody.

  • Kagha repented
    • Arabella lives, her parents live
      • Halsin allows Kagha to remain in the Grove, however she is demoted to novice. If the party returns to the area later in Act One, she stands on the path overlooking the grove -- near where Zevlor and Aradin fought when the party first arrived.)
    • Arabella died, her parents live
      • Halsin leaves her fate in  Locke and  Komira's hands. They attempt to poison Kagha at the party, which kills her unless the party intervene.
      • If the party can convince Locke and Komira to spare Kagha, the poison can be cured (e.g., with Lesser Restoration). Kagha thanks the party profusely and vows to improve herself.
  • Kagha did not repent
    • Arabella died, her parents live
      • Halsin leaves her fate in  Locke and  Komira's hands. They attempt to poison Kagha at the party, which kills her unless a party member intervenes.
      • If the player character convinces Locke and Komira to spare Kagha, the poison can be cured (e.g., with Lesser Restoration). Kagha then thanks the player character profusely and vows to improve herself.
    • Arabella and her Parents died
      • Kagha is exiled from the Emerald Grove, and all Groves of Silvanus.
    • Convinced to let Arabella go earlier
      • Kagha is demoted to the most junior rank of druid

Combat

Attacks and actions

Kagha has an ability kit similar to a Level 5 druid, including the ability to cast spells using Level 3 Spell Slots.[2]

 Cure Wounds ( + )
Healing: 1~8 + modifiers
1d8 + Spellcasting modifier⁠Healing
Heal a creature you can touch.
 Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft)
 Heat Metal ( + )
Damage: 2~16
2d8⁠Fire

Cause a metal weapon or armour to glow red-hot and force the wearer to let go or receive  Disadvantage on  Attack rolls and Ability Checks.

If the creature is only wearing metal armour, it always receives Disadvantage.
If the creature is still touching the metal, you can use a bonus action on subsequent turns to deal another 2d8⁠⁠Fire and force the creature to let go or receive Disadvantage.

 CON Save
 Range: 18 m (60 ft)
 Main Hand Attack ()   –  dagger
Damage: 4~7
1d4 + 3⁠Piercing
Make a melee attack with your equipped weapon.
 Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft)
 Misty Step ( + )

Surrounded by silver mist, you teleport to an unoccupied space you can see.

 Range: 18 m (60 ft)
 Moonbeam ( + )
Damage: 2~20
2d10⁠Radiant
Call down a beam of light that damages any creatures that enters the beam or starts its turn in the light. You can use an Action to move the beam 18 m (60 ft).
 CON Save
 Range: 18 m (60 ft)

Damage: 4~9
1d6 + 3⁠Slashing
Make a melee attack with your off-hand weapon.
 Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft)
 Plant Growth ( + )

Make weeds burst from the ground and smother the area. Creatures moving through the weeds have their Movement Speed quartered.

 Range: 18 m (60 ft)
 Thunderwave ( + )
Damage: 2~16
2d8⁠Thunder
Release a wave of thunderous force that pushes away all creatures and objects in an area, while also dealing Thunder damage.
 CON Save
 Melee: 1.5 m (5 ft)
 Wild Shape: Wolf ( + )

Assume the shape of a dire wolf that can  Incite allies and  Distract enemies. The dire wolf has a starting health of 18 hit points that increase every two druid levels.

While in animal shape, you can't talk or cast spells. You take on the attributes of your beast form - excluding your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.

When your beast form drops to 0 hit points, you revert to your normal form.

Speak with Dead

Kagha's corpse can be communed with using  Speak with Dead.

  • What happened to you? How did you come to die?
    • Kagha
      Punished for... protecting the grove...
  • From where do you hail?
    • Kagha
      Born to the circle... belonged to the circle...
  • What did you mean to accomplish in the grove?
    • Kagha
      Complete the Rite of Thorns... safe from the coming storm...
  • Why did you take the tiefling girl?
    • Kagha
      Stole the idol... needed for ritual... choice and consequence...
  • Why did you ally with the Shadow Druids?
    • Kagha
      The power to... protect my people... sanctuary...
  • Who were you in life? (If the party did not meet Kagha before her death)
    • Kagha
      Emerald Enclave... rightful First Druid...
  • This magic is ordered. Powerful. Someone gave it to you. Who? (If the interacting party member is a sorcerer)
    • Kagha
      In shadow... a gift from Cloakwood...
  • A rune is missing in the enclave library. Where can I find it? (If the party know that there is a missing rune in the Enclave Library)
    • Kagha
      Halsin... gave to Rath...

Notes and references

  1. ↑ "Ssifisv," the command she gives Teela, is a  Draconic command to step down.
  2. ↑ Kagha prioritizes maintaining Moonbeam above all other actions. This can often lead her to walk into her own Moonbeam. It can also cause the deaths of nearby NPCs with low HP such as Loic or Silver.
